statement: Suppose a projective birational morphism h : Y → X is a log model over a smooth curve as in Section 5.1, except that X → C need not be proper. Assume X and Y are quasi-projective, all exceptional prime divisors map into the section Γ ≃ C, and put A = KY + H − h∗ KX. 29 If Y0 = S0 + P a Sa and the nearby fibers are irreducible, then (A|Yc )2 = (A|S0 )2 + X a (A|Sa )2 . Under the full-boundary, adjunction, and nefness hypotheses of Proposition 7.2, the first two squares are respectively −β(Xc, Γ(c)) and −β(X0, Γ(0)), while (A|Sa )2 = (KSa + BSa )2 . Thus vanishing of the extra squares proves constancy of the local invariant without a projective compactification of X.
